title: What each module is for
intro: These 40 modules are components of one zeroned application: 23 custom modules and 17 SDK/IBC modules. The map describes this source build, not the installed binary or enabled paths on every network.

development.title: Development and design
development.scope: A source-build map, not a live health check. Implementation, network publication and accepted design are separate states; none of these labels authorizes activation.

tracks.title: Research workspace
tracks.purpose: Keep local contributions, evidence, revisions and divergent continuations; deliberately bind one selected assertion to a native review workflow.
tracks.next: Exercise the published handoff with a willing independently controlled reviewer and retain corrections and payment observations.
tracks.boundary: Browser journals stay local until downloaded or deliberately shared. Preparing a workflow file does not sign or submit a claim.

tracks.title: Shared development ledger
tracks.purpose: Run explicit signed claims, reasoned reviews and prefunded settlement on zerone-dev-1, separately from the legacy ledger.
tracks.next: Use the published participant package and verify its exact network pins before acting; retain the predecessor package for original-genesis replay.
tracks.boundary: The 23 September publication records knowledge version 11 at source 5542b221. GitHub-hosted participant files require repository access. This build does not recheck that runtime. Development funds have no monetary value and one operator initially produces blocks.

tracks.title: One owner for each authoritative state
tracks.purpose: Consolidate consensus stake in SDK staking, ordinary execution in SDK governance, and domain identity in ontology.
tracks.next: Reconcile custody and obligations, then implement and rehearse H4-F, H4 and H5 in their accepted dependency order.
tracks.boundary: Custom stake/governance and duplicate domain writers still exist. A name change or a single writer does not establish independent control or non-economic governance.

tracks.title: Retained machinery and research designs
tracks.purpose: Distinguish custody-bearing modules and existing block work from optional adapters, static diagrams and offline experiments.
tracks.next: Trace each consumer, callback and liability before moving analysis to clients or retiring a financial path. Use the module boundaries below.
tracks.boundary: Not all older machinery is inert: alignment pacing and ontology ceilings still affect knowledge. Static research publication does not activate rewards, authority or an external integration.

tracks.title: Legacy preservation and successor release
tracks.purpose: Preserve the legacy zerone-1 history while keeping its observer, shared development and the unactivated zerone-2 release kit distinct.
tracks.next: Use each network's compatible build and complete the separate custody, recovery and signed release gates before a successor activation.
tracks.boundary: Current main is not the legacy runtime. The zerone-2 kit remains NO-GO; website deployment changes neither validator software nor consensus authority.

modules.label: Knowledge
modules.purpose: Keep assertions, reasoned reviews, facts and their corrections together.
modules.owns: Claims, commit/reveal rounds, retained reviews, fact relations, recorded funding terms and pending settlement; also older training and ecology state.
modules.boundary: A recorded verdict is not scientific truth. Neutral reviews bypass older score weights, but ontology ceilings and alignment pacing still apply.

connections.why: Collect review funding and directly pay current reviewers, claim budgets and refunds.
Create or settle retained vesting schedules and deposit research funds; current review payments use bank directly.
Read domain rules and confidence ceilings; a separate knowledge domain registry still exists.
Read legacy qualification; current neutral policy selects a different review path.
Read validated counterexamples for legacy weighting.
Record and inspect capture-related review observations.
Read claim pacing, cooldown and fee inputs.
Notify the bridge when a claim round resolves.

modules.label: Ontology
modules.purpose: Give research domains names, structure and lifecycle rules.
modules.owns: Domain definitions, status and structure, strata, logic zones and confidence ceilings.
modules.boundary: The accepted target is one domain owner. Knowledge still maintains a second registry; reconciliation is unfinished.

connections.why: Supply domain rules; do not silently merge its separate registry.
Supply domain-depth information for qualification inheritance.

modules.label: Counterexamples
modules.purpose: Keep structured negative examples and their validation records.
modules.owns: Counterexample entries anchored to existing facts and separate validation votes.
modules.boundary: These records are distinct from a native knowledge contradiction or challenge; they also feed a legacy weighting path.

connections.why: Check that a cited fact exists and expose validated-example status.

modules.label: Qualification
modules.purpose: Record bounded evidence and credentials for work in a domain.
modules.owns: Qualifications, endorsements, legacy weights and stake escrow.
modules.boundary: Stake-based qualification still exists. Neutral review does not use its legacy weights; the direct capture-defense input is not wired.

connections.why: Read domain-depth differences for qualification inheritance.
Receive consequences of upheld capture cases.

modules.label: Training provenance
modules.purpose: Assemble provenance views from the scientific and review records.
modules.owns: No separate ledger; derives certificates and query responses from other modules.
modules.boundary: A derived certificate describes recorded provenance; it does not prove an artifact was used in training.

modules.label: SDK accounts
modules.purpose: Represent accounts that can authorize transactions.
modules.owns: Public keys, account numbers, sequence numbers and module-account permissions.
modules.boundary: Private keys stay with the signer. Zerone auth adds metadata and controls; it does not replace SDK account semantics.

connections.why: Associate balances and module custody with accounts.
Complement account signing with participant metadata and controls.

modules.label: SDK bank
modules.purpose: Keep the canonical balances and supply of coins.
modules.owns: Transfers and permissioned module mint/burn operations; other modules keep the claims against their custody.
modules.boundary: A module balance alone does not identify its creditors or make money available to spend.

connections.why: Provide balances used by custom settlement and mint-cap callers.

modules.label: SDK account vesting
modules.purpose: Apply time-based spending locks to vesting accounts.
modules.owns: SDK vesting-account behavior over account balances.
modules.boundary: This is separate from the schedules and reserves in vesting_rewards.

modules.label: Zerone auth
modules.purpose: Bind participant metadata and controls to authenticated accounts.
modules.owns: Human/agent registration, DID and key bindings, rotations, freezes and capabilities.
modules.boundary: A DID or extra account does not establish one independent controller, expertise or consent to another action.

connections.why: Supplement SDK account signatures and sequence checks.
Supply registration information for its admission rules.

modules.label: Home
modules.purpose: Keep agent-home, session and notification references.
modules.owns: Home ownership, sessions and keys, guardian alerts and memory references.
modules.boundary: A memory reference does not store its target content or establish an agent identity.

connections.why: Use bank-backed operations where the home contract requires them.

modules.label: SDK distribution
modules.purpose: Distribute consensus fees and rewards to validators and delegators.
modules.owns: Validator commission, delegator rewards and withdrawal addresses.
modules.boundary: Research review payments use separate funding and settlement records.

connections.why: Read consensus delegation and validator state.
Distribute the fee remainder after custom fee routing.

modules.label: SDK fee allowances
modules.purpose: Let an account explicitly pay another account’s transaction fees.
modules.owns: Fee allowance grants and limits consumed by transaction admission.
modules.boundary: Fee sponsorship does not fund a research bounty or certify the transaction’s content.

connections.why: Pay transaction fees through the ante handler.

modules.label: Vesting and settlement
modules.purpose: Keep explicit payment schedules, releases and shared funding controls.
modules.owns: Vesting escrow, reserves, fee routing, research funds and the mint-cap gate used by its callers.
modules.boundary: Automatic block/founder issuance is retired. A schedule or failed payment attempt is not a completed transfer.

connections.why: Read survival telemetry and adjudicated disproof for FalsifyClaim; receive retained schedules and research-fund deposits.
Route research/development fee slices before SDK distribution consumes the remainder.

modules.label: Work sponsorship
modules.purpose: Fund specified work from a sponsor’s existing money.
modules.owns: Bounty orders, escrow, fulfillment, sponsor vetoes and refunds.
modules.boundary: This spends existing supply and never mints. It is separate from feegrant and from native review fees.

connections.why: Escrow, pay or refund the sponsor’s funds.
Read cited fact status, domain and submission time.

modules.label: Claiming pots
modules.purpose: Apply the existing bootstrap and general-pot admission rules.
modules.owns: Pot claims and their mint requests.
modules.boundary: A contribution alone does not create a claim on a pot. Existing claims need reconciliation before retirement.

modules.label: Issued and wrapped tokens
modules.purpose: Manage additional issued assets and wrapping contracts.
modules.owns: Asset metadata, allowances, backing and optional emission periods.
modules.boundary: These are additional products; native bank balances do not depend on using them. Native emission periods default to disabled.

connections.why: Hold backing and transfer or mint permitted assets.

modules.label: Liquidity pools
modules.purpose: Run pools, swaps and their ownership accounting.
modules.owns: Pool reserves, LP shares, exits and time-weighted price records.
modules.boundary: Its bank adapter may mint only canonical pool-share denominations. Reserve and bearer claims must survive any retirement.

connections.why: Hold reserves, settle swaps and issue restricted LP shares.

modules.label: Genesis transactions
modules.purpose: Initialize the chain from accounts and genesis transactions.
modules.owns: Genesis transaction execution, including initial SDK validator setup.
modules.boundary: Genesis initialization is not an ongoing account-admission or validator-joining service.

connections.why: Apply initial validator and delegation transactions.

modules.label: SDK consensus staking
modules.purpose: Own the validator set and stake that determine consensus voting power.
modules.owns: Consensus validators, delegations, unbonding and validator updates.
modules.boundary: Custom zerone_staking is a separate application ledger and does not itself grant consensus power.

connections.why: Supply bonded voting weight to current SDK governance.
Notify reward accounting through staking hooks.
Notify consensus signing and penalty tracking.

modules.label: Consensus slashing
modules.purpose: Apply consensus signing and liveness consequences.
modules.owns: Signing information, missed-block tracking and consensus-fault penalties.
modules.boundary: This concerns block production, not research judgment or capture-challenge outcomes.

connections.why: Jail or slash consensus validators where the protocol requires it.

modules.label: Consensus evidence
modules.purpose: Process evidence of consensus misbehavior.
modules.owns: Consensus misbehavior evidence and its handling.
modules.boundary: This is not the evidence attached to a research claim or counterexample.

modules.label: Consensus parameters
modules.purpose: Store the consensus parameters used by the application.
modules.owns: CometBFT consensus parameter state connected to BaseApp.
modules.boundary: Consensus on chain state does not decide whether a scientific proposition is true.

connections.why: Use application authority for permitted parameter updates.

modules.label: Upgrade lifecycle
modules.purpose: Apply named software and store migrations at explicit boundaries.
modules.owns: Scheduled upgrade plans, applied-plan records and module-version handoff.
modules.boundary: The application requires explicit cancellation before replacing an existing plan. A published binary alone does not activate an upgrade.

connections.why: Run the ordered pre-block handoff before account processing.

modules.label: SDK governance
modules.purpose: Execute ordinary SDK proposals through the application’s authority.
modules.owns: SDK proposals, deposits, stake-weighted tally and typed execution, including software upgrades.
modules.boundary: Current SDK voting still uses stake, and custom governance remains alongside it. Accepted authority consolidation is unfinished.

connections.why: Read the post-incident hold that restricts ordinary SDK governance after quarantine ends; not a shared stake ledger or executor.

modules.label: Custom LIP governance
modules.purpose: Manage custom LIP proposals and separate research-fund decisions.
modules.owns: Custom proposals, stake ballots, phases, seats, deposits and research-fund spending.
modules.boundary: Separate from SDK governance, which alone schedules upgrades. The app's parameter router has no registered handlers; creed amendment and adapter-registration paths are incomplete. LIP resolution does not refund deposits: aggregate escrow lacks individual contributor records.

connections.why: Hold LIP deposits in custody and read research-fund balances.
Attached amendment primitive; category configuration and two-pool tally remain incomplete.
Attachment only: legacy tally records an inert pass; accounting-safety tally refuses adapter registration.

modules.label: Custom participation staking
modules.purpose: Keep the older application participation and stake records.
modules.owns: Custom profiles, delegations, unbonding claims and separate stake custody.
modules.boundary: These records are distinct from SDK consensus validators. Preserve individual claims before consolidating or closing them.

connections.why: Hold custom delegation and exit custody.

modules.label: Emergency recovery
modules.purpose: Constrain transactions and coordinate explicit recovery procedures.
modules.owns: Guardian ceremonies, quarantine, reopening and recovery authorization records.
modules.boundary: Quarantine does not itself stop consensus. Recovery is not a second ordinary governance or treasury path.

connections.why: Validate recovery proposals and restrict SDK governance execution.
Check exact upgrade targets for recovery authorization.

modules.label: Capture observations
modules.purpose: Track concentration and feed the existing capture-response rules.
modules.owns: Domain concentration metrics, reputation observations, flags and automatic challenge triggers.
modules.boundary: Address concentration does not prove independent controllers. Its effects remain part of consensus behavior.

connections.why: Read domain depth for the existing HHI threshold.
Read review activity and receive review observations.
Open cases under the existing flag rules.
Read analysis pacing; capture flags are not wired back into alignment's security sensor.

modules.label: Capture disputes
modules.purpose: Keep capture cases and settle their bounded consequences.
modules.owns: Cases, challenge bonds, refunds and outcomes. It requests qualification penalties and knowledge-threshold changes stored by those modules.
modules.boundary: A metric-driven case is not an independent finding about a person’s identity or worth.

connections.why: Receive metrics/evidence pushed into automatic challenges and clear flags on rejection. RunRiskAnalysis is a no-op; the challenge adapter's GetCaptureMetrics accessor has no production caller.

modules.label: Health and pacing
modules.purpose: Record application health and supply the existing pacing rules.
modules.owns: Health observations and advisory corrections; pacing affects claim cooldowns, minimum fees and capture processing.
modules.boundary: Its direct capture-flag sensor is disconnected. Corrections are advisory; restoring a missing input could still change pacing and voting behavior.

connections.why: Supply pacing; the reverse flagged-domain sensor is not wired.
Supply health inputs for expedited voting.

modules.label: Derived trust views
modules.purpose: Offer optional derived views of recorded review and qualification history.
modules.owns: No separate ledger; combines observations from existing state.
modules.boundary: A derived score does not establish a person’s worth, identity or independent governing authority.

modules.label: Creed document pins
modules.purpose: Keep versioned commitments to creed documents.
modules.owns: Append-only document pins and council records.
modules.boundary: A hash commits to bytes; it neither stores the document nor proves agreement. Direct authority anchoring differs from the incomplete amendment dispatch path.

connections.why: Use the SDK governance module account as authority.
Expose the amendment primitive, not a complete custom-governance amendment workflow.

modules.label: Work-creed pins
modules.purpose: Preserve sub-creed commitments supplied at genesis.
modules.owns: A registry of genesis-supplied artifact pins.
modules.boundary: There is no current transaction, query or amendment API; default genesis is empty.

modules.label: External-work attestations
modules.purpose: Bind externally performed work and adapter provenance to existing scientific records.
modules.owns: Adapter revisions, attestations, bonds, delayed settlement and retained legacy pending-claim links.
modules.boundary: It does not fetch evidence or execute adapter compilers. Cited facts must already exist; witness-only links are allowed and new pending claims are rejected.

connections.why: Use SDK governance authority for adapter-management messages.
Read cited facts and receive callbacks for retained pending links.
Check attestation submitter credentials against the adapter’s requirements.

modules.label: IBC protocol
modules.purpose: Verify and route interchain protocol packets.
modules.owns: Client, connection, channel and packet state.
modules.boundary: Registration does not establish enabled routes, open channels, independent peers or a funded connection.

modules.label: IBC token transfer
modules.purpose: Move fungible assets through ICS-20 escrow and vouchers.
modules.owns: Transfer escrow and denomination/voucher tracking.
modules.boundary: Interchain transfer is separate from custom token issuance and LP-share policy.

connections.why: Escrow native assets and mint or burn transfer vouchers.

modules.label: IBC accounts
modules.purpose: Support ICS-27 controller and host account execution across chains.
modules.owns: Remote-account controller and host protocol state under one registered module.
modules.boundary: This is not human identity or private-key custody. Available messages and routes depend on the network configuration.

connections.why: Use local accounts for permitted host execution.

modules.label: IBC Tendermint light client
modules.purpose: Verify headers and proofs from a remote CometBFT chain.
modules.owns: Light-client consensus state and verification logic through IBC.
modules.boundary: A remote light client does not create a local consensus validator.

modules.label: IBC solo-machine light client
modules.purpose: Verify signed state and proofs from an IBC solo machine.
modules.owns: Solo-machine client state and signature verification through IBC.
modules.boundary: This is a remote proof mechanism, not local block consensus or participant identity.

modules.label: IBC transfer limits
modules.purpose: Bound traffic through the IBC token-transfer path.
modules.owns: Rate-limit parameters and traffic accounting for transfer middleware.
modules.boundary: This protection wraps transfer; it is not a blanket claim that every IBC route is covered.

connections.why: Wrap inbound and outbound token-transfer processing.

workflow.title: Record
workflow.text: Keep questions, methods, evidence and revisions in a local research journal. Choose what to publish; importing a file does not create chain state.

workflow.title: Claim
workflow.text: Select one exact contribution and prepare its claim intent. Your pinned participant client signs explicit admission; knowledge records the assertion and funding terms.

workflow.title: Review
workflow.text: Reviewers choose their own judgment, reason and evidence, then commit and reveal with their own keys. Current neutral policy counts admitted accounts equally; that does not establish independent controllers.

workflow.title: Correction
workflow.text: Keep journal corrections as new records. A native contradiction or challenge is a separate signed action naming an actual Fact; earlier claims and reviews remain in history. The counterexamples module keeps a separate structured-example record.

workflow.title: Funding and settlement
workflow.text: Inspect the recorded budget, review fees, pending obligations, completed payments and refunds separately. A schedule is not a payment; sponsorship is a separate funded-work contract.

boundaries.title: Keep the owner visible
boundaries.text: SDK bank owns coin balances; SDK staking owns consensus voting power. Custom staking and governance still coexist with SDK paths, and knowledge and ontology still have separate domain registries. The accepted single-owner migration is unfinished.

boundaries.title: Trace effects before reconnecting
boundaries.text: Alignment pacing, capture challenges and older economic paths can affect fees, thresholds or money. A disconnected input is not permission to reactivate it as a cosmetic wiring fix.

boundaries.title: Use the appropriate lane
boundaries.text: Local records stay in files. Shared development accepts explicit participant actions under its published rules. Legacy zerone-1 uses a different binary lineage; module registration alone does not establish live availability.

sharedUtilities.label: x/common
sharedUtilities.text: Shared types and helpers; not another registered module.

sharedUtilities.label: x/witness
sharedUtilities.text: An unregistered admission implementation; its presence in source does not add a running app module.

sharedUtilities.label: Journal and participant tools
sharedUtilities.text: Local file preparation and explicit signed-client use sit outside ModuleManager. They connect a chosen record to an admitted claim without turning every note into chain state.
